action: Customers of JPMorgan and Mastercard benefit programs: expect phishing that uses your name or email, and do not act on unsolicited messages.
date_note: The article's publication date was not visible; it refers to the JPMorgan outage of November 16, so November 17 is the best supported day.
exec: Vendor breach exposed marketing data at major payment and banking brands; phishing risk for customers.
plain: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard say outside vendors were hacked. JPMorgan and Mastercard say some customer email addresses may be exposed; they say card payment data was not.
summary: The n0n extortion gang listed Visa and JPMorgan Chase as victims. Visa says the claims relate to a third-party provider in Asia Pacific. Yahoo Finance reports JPMorgan believes attackers accessed marketing data at its vendors, possibly customer names and email addresses, and Mastercard cites limited cardholder email addresses. The companies say payments data and their own systems were not affected; n0n attribution comes from SOCRadar.
title: Visa says incident was at an Asia Pacific third-party provider after n0n gang lists it and JPMorgan
